The customer’s question

“Does this transistor leak too much electricity when it’s supposed to be off?”

A transistor is an electronic switch. Even when it is off, a small current can still flow. This demo checks that current against an agreed limit.

WHY THIS MATTERS

Get from a vague request to a defensible decision.

An engineer needs the right test, the right conditions, and evidence for the limit. This workflow makes those decisions visible.

How the workflow earns trust

Retrieve before answering. Find the relevant technical source and show where the information came from.

Clarify before acting. Missing values stay unresolved until a person supplies or approves them.

This prototype uses document retrieval and explicit rules. The test runs use synthetic readings. No live language model or physical tester is connected.

Research question, measured results, and next experiment.

PROBLEM DEFINITION

Can terminology-aware retrieval recover useful evidence?

Engineers describe the same test differently. This experiment compares token overlap, BM25 ranking, and BM25 with a small explicit terminology map on identical queries.

Success criteria

Find labeled evidence in the top three results, preserve source identity, flag ambiguous requests, and block incomplete simulated procedures. The simulator must switch output off after acquisition and compliance faults.

What is implemented

Browser-based lexical retrieval, transparent alias expansion, deterministic test-family classification, structured validation, cited evidence, plan export, Python simulation, and an executable evaluation harness.

RESEARCH INTEGRITY

Development results, not independent validation

The author constructed both the terminology map and the benchmark. Paraphrases are clustered for bootstrap resampling. This controls one source of dependence but does not eliminate author bias or establish industrial performance.

All benchmark requests and all simulated measurements are synthetic. No engineer time savings, physical measurement accuracy, or production readiness is claimed.

Next experiment

Freeze the retriever and collect unseen engineer-authored requests. Have an electrical engineer independently label evidence and review plans. Compare answer correctness and task completion time using a randomized, counterbalanced study.

Optional language model

The Python adapter supports a user-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It receives retrieved evidence and must return cited JSON. Its output is experimental; the hosted demo does not call it, and reported results do not evaluate it.

Data provenance

Evidence records are short editorial paraphrases, manually linked to publisher documents and sections. Full-document ingestion is available as a local utility but was not used in these benchmark results. Publisher PDFs are not redistributed.
